📝 Notes
Feb 9, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Noémi Biró voiced concerns regarding ownership and compensation for their significant involvement in the Cibil project, arguing for public recognition and a compensation structure, like a percentage of ownership applicable upon acquisition, should Cibil successfully exit. The team primarily discussed two potential solutions: joining Cibil as full-time founders or, preferably, delivering the initial four months of work followed by a discussion for continued, compensated involvement, potentially at a technical advisory level. The participants decided to discuss the acquisition process and continued collaboration, framed as a transition to an equity-based consultancy role, with Melissa in a future meeting to establish a clear path forward after the initial four months of work.
Details
Ownership and Compensation Concerns with Cibil Noémi Biró raised concerns about a feeling of ownership in the Cibil project not being reflected in the current agreement, driven by excitement about Cibil's prospects and their significant involvement. They highlighted the need for compensation if Cibil successfully exits, such as through acquisition (00:00:00), and also emphasized the necessity for public recognition and credit for the work done by body lab (00:01:52).
Potential Solutions for Ownership and Involvement Multiple scenarios were discussed as solutions, with Noémi Biró outlining two main options: joining Cibil as full-time founders and giving up on the Ambodi project, which was deemed too early and potentially overstaffed for Cibil at the current scale, despite overlaps in interest (00:01:52); and the preferred approach of delivering the agreed-upon four months of work and then discussing continued involvement, potentially at a technical advisory level, in exchange for a percentage of ownership. This ownership could be defined to apply only in case of an acquisition (00:03:20).
Connecting Post-Four-Month Involvement with Ownership The team discussed whether ownership should be tied to the substantial work completed during the initial four months or to the continuous commitment afterward. Noémi Biró argued that the ownership should be tied to continuous commitment and involvement, though acknowledged that the four months of work lay the foundation for Cibil (00:07:08) (00:09:14). They proposed bringing up the topic of continued involvement and ownership during the next meeting regarding the agreement, framing it as compensation for ongoing technical advisory (00:05:35).
Strategy for Discussing Future Involvement and Acquisition The team decided to bring up the topic of continued collaboration and potential acquisition scenarios as an open discussion with Melissa (00:13:54) (00:22:16). Noémi Biró suggested asking Melissa how she views the acquisition process and the team's involvement, particularly in a very close future (e.g., within six to nine months), to plant a seed for future considerations (00:15:31) (00:19:14). This approach aims to secure a clear path for continued collaboration after the initial four months, possibly evolving into an equity-based consultancy role rather than just being compensated as a company (00:18:04).
Balancing Cibil Commitment with Ambodi Projects The discussion highlighted the need to use the four-month period to gain clarity and reassess their position, including pursuing other opportunities and internal projects under Ambodi (00:20:31). Noémi Biró stated that the team could always offer ongoing support to Cibil, regardless of the success of their own internal projects, by scaling up capacity or finding personnel if their own business becomes very successful (00:24:21).
Suggested next steps
Noémi Biró will bring up the general topic of ownership and continuous technical advisory in the next meeting to finalize the agreement.
The group will help Melissa find a CTO and show good intention while still discussing the potential for ongoing support after the four-month contract.
The group will bring up the topic with Melissa to discuss what happens after the four months of collaboration, including how she sees the process and the group's involvement if Cibil is about to be acquired.
The group will keep an eye on the question of continued involvement and ownership with Cibil and keep bringing it up to Melissa throughout the four months.
